authors: Claude Code session (holant lead, step b)

links.note: Step (b) as worded compares tensor/flattening ranks of T after invertible bond-wise basis changes; those ranks are GL-invariant (invariance.py, all flattening ranks 61 at p=61 under Fourier, multiplicative-character and random bases), so the step is reformulated with a basis-dependent measure: QTT ranks over the binary digits of the F_p alphabet.

question: For the decomposition transfer matrix M[y,z] = #{x in FB : S_3(x,y,z)=0} over F_p (p < 2^L, L = 6..10), is the binary-digit tensor-train (QTT) rank of M under the natural x-coordinate labelling lower than under a uniformly random relabelling of F_p, i.e. do x-coordinates carry digit-level structure that a poly(log p) contraction could use?

claims.text: Flattening and CP ranks of T are invariant under invertible bond-wise basis changes, so the original step (b) cannot discriminate (theorem; numerical identity check in invariance.py).
At p <= 2^10, the interleaved QTT rank r_max of M in x-labelling is (or is not) below the random-relabelling null, by the preregistered rule.
claims.if_supported: first non-generic digit-level structure in the x-labelled network; next step is a charged comparison against matched rho on a size ladder
claims.if_not_supported: no digit-level QTT structure at p <= 2^10; the lead's step (b) records exhausted_at_scale for this measure, reopening only for a labelling or basis family with sub-polynomial description in p

hypotheses.statement: x-coordinate labelling hides the Cayley-graph structure as well as a random labelling does (QTT ranks of M in x-labelling match the random-relabelling null).
hypotheses.mechanism: x(P) for P in a cyclic group of prime order behaves like a pseudo-random function of log P; digit structure of x carries no information about the group law beyond the algebraic relation S_3.

predictions.minimum_effect: X inside the null's central 90% on >= 7 of 9 curves with L >= 8

arms.description: M with natural x-coordinate labelling 0..p-1, padded to 2^L
M relabelled by a uniform random permutation of F_p; 99 draws per curve; draws split into streams 0/1 by parity for the A/A check
E-block of M relabelled by discrete-log orbit index min(k, n-k) - 1 (a Toeplitz-plus-Hankel pattern in that order); twist x's keep natural order after it
shift matrix [z = y + 1 mod p], a known low-QTT-rank object, run through the same rank code

positive.expected_detection: LOG r_max below the minimum null r_max on every curve with L >= 8; SH reported as detector sanity

null_population.description: uniform random relabellings of F_p applied to the same M of the same curve
null_population.why_n: min one-sided empirical p 0.01 per curve; the SIGNAL rule conjoins 9 curves

factors.name: curve
factors.how: 3 curves per size, (a,b) drawn from a stream seeded by sha256(protocol_sha|curves|L); accepted iff nonsingular and #E(F_p) an odd prime

factors.name: factor_base
factors.value: floor(sqrt p) smallest x-coordinates of E(F_p)
factors.how: same FB for all arms of a curve

factors.name: generator_for_LOG
factors.how: orbit index is generator-dependent only up to a multiplier; fixed rule

factors.name: rank_tolerance
factors.how: same numeric rank rule in every unfolding of every arm

factors.name: padding
factors.value: zero-pad p x p to 2^L x 2^L, labels 0..p-1 occupy the low indices

factors.name: host
factors.how: counts only; host recorded in the export, no clock read

randomization.arm_order_reason: ranks are exact deterministic counts of a fixed matrix; execution order cannot change them (no clock, no state carried between arms)

seed_derivation.note: every seed is sha256(freeze.protocol_sha256 | tag | L | curve | draw)[:8]; the hash is passed as --protocol-sha

instance_sampling.rule: curves drawn before and independently of any arm

blinding.how: analysis is a frozen script applying a fixed rule; no analyst choice remains

power.note: the SIGNAL rule is one conjunctive test: X below all 99 null draws on all 9 curves with L >= 8 (null probability <= 0.01^9). The intended effect is large (a usable structure would need r_max far below the ~2^L null), so 99 draws per curve resolve it; a subtle effect is out of scope.

preflight_runtime.measured_on: this container; p=1021 build 0.55 s + ranks 2.36 s, p=251 0.22 s, on a curve drawn with a non-sample seed tag (timing only, ranks not read)

primary.name: max interleaved QTT rank
primary.definition: max over the 2L-1 unfoldings of M (digits y_msb,z_msb,...,y_0,z_0) of the numeric rank

secondary.name: max blocked QTT rank
secondary.definition: same, digits ordered y then z

secondary.name: sum of log2 ranks
secondary.definition: sum over cuts of log2 rank (interleaved and blocked)

stopping_rules.rule: fixed design: 5 sizes x 3 curves x (X, LOG, SH, 99 N) = 1530 matrices, then stop

decision_rule.text: Validity: LOG r_max < min null r_max on every curve with L >= 8, and |median(stream0) - median(stream1)| <= pooled null IQR on every such curve; otherwise INVALID_CONTROLS. SIGNAL: X r_max below every null draw on all 9 curves with L >= 8 and X r_max <= 0.75 x null median on every L = 10 curve. NULL: X inside the null's 5th..95th percentile on >= 7 of those 9 curves. Otherwise INCONCLUSIVE. (C-aa is a validity gate, not a deciding comparison.)
decision_rule.statistic: interleaved r_max per curve; empirical one-sided p = (1 + #null <= X)/100

inadmissible: changing sizes, curves, FB rule, null draws, rank tolerance or the decision rule after seeing results
reading a SIGNAL as an attack-cost claim: QTT rank of M is a structure statistic, not a priced method
excluding a curve or a null draw after seeing its rank
